topicName: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) and XML External Entity (XXE)
content:
[{"order":1,"heading":"heading","text":"Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) and XML External Entity (XXE) Tutorial"},{"order":2,"heading":"subheading","text":"Introduction to SSRF and XXE"},{"order":3,"heading":"paragraph","text":"Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) and XML External Entity (XXE) injection are critical vulnerabilities that occur when applications improperly handle user-supplied input to fetch external resources or parse structured XML data. Ethical hackers must understand these mechanisms to secure modern web architectures against unauthorized internal access and data disclosure."},{"order":4,"heading":"subheading","text":"Understanding SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery)"},{"order":5,"heading":"paragraph","text":"SSRF allows an attacker to induce the application server to make HTTP requests to an arbitrary domain of the attacker's choosing. This often bypasses firewalls or network access controls, allowing access to internal services like metadata APIs (e.g., AWS 169.254.169.254) or local databases."},{"order":6,"heading":"code","text":"GET /fetch?url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable-app.com"},{"order":7,"heading":"subheading","text":"Common SSRF Mitigation Techniques"},{"order":8,"heading":"bullet_point","text":"Implement a whitelist of allowed domains and URI schemes (e.g., allow only HTTPS and specific trusted APIs)."},{"order":9,"heading":"bullet_point","text":"Disable unnecessary URL schemes such as file://, gopher://, and dict:// in the underlying HTTP client libraries."},{"order":10,"heading":"bullet_point","text":"Isolate the application server network tier using strict egress filtering and firewalls."},{"order":11,"heading":"subheading","text":"Understanding XXE (XML External Entity)"},{"order":12,"heading":"paragraph","text":"XXE occurs when XML input containing a reference to an external entity is processed by a weakly configured XML parser. This vulnerability can lead to the disclosure of confidential files, internal port scanning, remote code execution, and Denial of Service (DoS)."},{"order":13,"heading":"code","text":"<?xml version="1.0" encoding="ISO-8859-1"?>
<!DOCTYPE foo [
  <!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">
]>
<stockCheck><productId>&xxe;</productId></stockCheck>"},{"order":14,"heading":"subheading","text":"Mitigating XXE Vulnerabilities"},{"order":15,"heading":"bullet_point","text":"Disable DTDs (Document Type Definitions) entirely if the application does not require them."},{"order":16,"heading":"bullet_point","text":"Disable external entity resolution and general entities in the XML parser configuration."},{"order":17,"heading":"bullet_point","text":"Use safer data formats like JSON instead of XML when handling complex API payloads."},{"order":18,"heading":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":19,"heading":"paragraph","text":"Both SSRF and XXE exploit the server's trust in external data or protocols. By implementing strict input validation, proper parsing configurations, and network isolation, security professionals can effectively defend applications against these high-severity threats."}]
